GUARD SELECTION DEFECT FIXED AND VALIDATED.
Root shape: findings are per-FILE, markers arrive per-COLLECTED-ITEM, so a hazard owned by an
UNCOLLECTED test could never reach its own opt-out. Fix distinguishes the two cases properly —
each finding now records is_test, and scoping happens BEFORE excusing:
 - a test-owned finding is in scope only when its own function is in the collected set; if not
   collected it is out of scope entirely (not excused), which is what makes the marker reachable;
 - a helper-owned finding has no test name, so it belongs to the file and is excused file-scope.
Verified truth table (8 rows) incl. the two directions that matter: owner collected+unmarked FAILS;
only-an-unrelated-clean-test PASSES; unmarked HELPER hazard still FAILS even when only a clean test
is collected.
Validation: guard oracle 27/27; the reproducer
'pytest tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py::test_long_matching_line_is_truncated' now RUNS
(1 passed); whole file 48 passed; --collect-only tests/unit exit 0.
Accepted deviation: tests/_subprocess_isolation.py now 519 lines (19 over the 200-500 target, far
under the 800 cap); the growth is the attribution rationale written into the code so the next reader
does not reintroduce the bug. Kept.
Tier census moved 24 -> 25 hazards because another change landed in the shared tree mid-work.

COORDINATION HAZARD I CREATED, RECORDED: I had TWO implementation subagents editing ONE worktree
concurrently (the parity amend and the backtest extension). The guard agent correctly refused to fix
lint errors in scripts/_backtest/stats.py (E501) and backtest_bugfix_size.py (I001) because git
status showed them as another change's in-flight work. That is exactly the 'two sessions writing into
one worktree' pattern read (b) documented as a structural Verified-1 generator. It cost nothing here
only because the agent was careful. Not repeating it: from here, one implementation agent at a time
in this worktree, and I will run make lint only when no agent is mid-edit.
